rv.q: My bet is that you're looking at a long-running West End smash.
this show is pure magic, the height of theatrical entertainment and it may even change your life
This is the new Mary Poppins: a well-known story imaginatively staged, immaculately performed and utterly winning.
Is this a new classic on a par with Mary Poppins or Matilda?
Those few flaws aside, the bear captures our hearts.

Furry, funny and fully-formed, the much-anticipated “Paddington” musical has finally arrived in the West End and it’s alive not only with joy but that vanishingly rare theatrical quality: completely beguiling charm.
Every detail of this show is exquisite – and I confidently predict that this will be one proudly British export that will go on to conquer the world.
Like a big game hunter, it aims at huge moving targets – and hits them, again and again.
It wants you to love it, and it is ultimately impossible to resist.
Well, it involves ingenious craft and collaboration, but the all-important result is that the West End’s Paddington is pure theatre magic.
It is irresistible; delicious and guilt-free.
And the production becomes intensely moving by the end.
But whatever the faults of the show, it’s sweeter than a marmalade sandwich, and if the cuddly creation at its heart doesn’t make it a hit, I’ll eat his hat.

Paddington’s story has been adapted for the stage by Jessica Swale with such care, it feels impossible to imagine any way this could have been done better. All of the heart and warmth you would associate with Paddington are all here in great supply, along with some fresh ideas that feel fitting for the theatre.
How glad I am to be wrong, because this show is simply wonderful.
The Musical achieves, however, is something far more ambitious: a musical that honours Michael Bond’s creation while speaking to contemporary audiences with wit, warmth and sophistication.
If it's not a huge commercial hit, I will eat my explorer's hat.
First of all, the show is sensational.
It is beyond brilliant. I suspended all disbelief.
Calling the musical 'unashamedly whimsical and charming', he praised its 'deft and daft use of fourth-wall breaking comedy'
That’s their problem, frankly, as there’s much to admire in this stunning and delightful show.
Paddington The Musical is a delightful, high-energy adventure celebrating the possibility of personal change.

You can barely take your eye off the genial little bear as he draws on comedy (darting around knocking over crockery) and heartstrings (his song The Explorer & The Bear is one of the wonderfully tender moments).
There is a buzz of anticipation, the set warmly overwhelms while the projected graphics slink off the stage and along the walls to bring the Savoy Theatre to life.
